project.title: Ninth Atlas Residences
project.subtitle: A story-led cinematic residential walkthrough
project.styleLock: Photorealistic premium architectural film experienced as one continuous prospective-buyer visit. Preserve the supplied architecture, furniture, materials, lighting language and spatial scale. Camera motion must be slow, stabilized and physically plausible. Maintain warm refined luxury, believable human activity and continuity of time-of-day. No warping, morphing, fantasy architecture, sudden geometry changes, furniture mutation, random signage, new text, unrelated skyline substitutions, aggressive camera moves or surreal transitions.

scenes.name: Aerial Project Establish
scenes.prompt: Opening shot of the exact residential campus in the reference. The camera behaves like a premium drone, beginning high and wide and gliding slowly forward and slightly downward toward the main arrival axis. Preserve every tower, landscaped court, road, pool and amenity relationship. Golden-hour light, subtle atmospheric depth, tiny restrained human and vehicle activity, elegant real-estate campaign cinematography. End with the entrance axis visually centered so the next shot can continue the buyer journey toward the property.

scenes.name: Boulevard Approach
scenes.prompt: Continue directly from the aerial as though the prospective buyer is now approaching the property at ground level. Preserve the exact entrance architecture, tower identity, landscape and materials in the reference. Execute a slow stabilized forward glide along the driveway toward the covered arrival zone, with only subtle vehicle movement and gentle foliage motion. Keep vertical architecture stable and premium. End closer to the porte-cochere and drop-off so the next shot feels like the same arrival continuing.

scenes.name: Arrival and Drop-off
scenes.prompt: Treat the supplied drop-off image as the exact continuation of the same visit. Glide slowly forward behind and slightly to the side of the arriving car toward the illuminated entrance. Preserve canopy geometry, columns, water features, glazing, landscaping, vehicle scale and people already present. Human movement must be minimal and natural. Finish oriented toward the pedestrian path into the building, preparing a seamless transition to the podium and lobby threshold.

scenes.name: Podium Transition
scenes.prompt: Continue from the drop-off into the exact covered podium transition shown in the reference. The camera moves at a calm walking pace from the vehicle side onto the polished pedestrian path and toward the glass lobby entrance. Preserve the wood ceiling, stone columns, planters, fountains, cars, lobby glazing and people. Reflections and water should move naturally. End just outside the lobby doors with the reception visible ahead, creating a clear hand-off to the interior lobby shot.

scenes.name: Main Lobby Entry
scenes.prompt: Enter the exact luxury lobby in the reference from the threshold, continuing the prospective buyer journey. Use a slow eye-level push toward reception with a subtle rightward drift that reveals the seating area, feature wall and circulation route. Preserve stone, timber, sculpture, furniture, plants, staff and lighting exactly. Keep people understated and realistic. Finish pointing toward the private residential circulation so the next scene naturally becomes the lift lobby and corridor.

scenes.name: Lift Lobby and Private Corridor
scenes.prompt: Use the exact lift lobby and private corridor shown in the reference. Begin near the elevators and glide forward at human walking pace down the corridor toward the apartment doors and distant window. Preserve bronze lift doors, wall panels, artwork, runner rugs, console, flowers, room numbers, lighting and corridor geometry. No people are needed. No text or numbering should change. Finish approaching the residential door zone, ready to enter the apartment in the next shot.

scenes.name: Apartment Foyer to Living Reveal
scenes.prompt: This is the first reveal inside the residence. Begin from the exact doorway and foyer viewpoint in the reference and make a slow stabilized push into the living room, as though the buyer has just entered the apartment. Preserve door, console, wall finishes, seating, coffee table, television, dining glimpse, balcony doors and skyline. Add only subtle curtain and foliage motion. Finish deeper inside the living area with the dining room visible to the right, setting up the next transition.

scenes.name: Living to Dining Transition
scenes.prompt: Continue through the same apartment without a visual reset. Start from the living-room side of the exact reference and perform a slow lateral-forward glide toward the dining area, keeping the balcony and skyline as a continuity anchor. Preserve sofa, rug, tables, chairs, artwork, lighting, flooring and room proportions. The movement should feel like a guided walkthrough, not a commercial orbit. Finish beside the dining table with the kitchen visible beyond.

scenes.name: Dining to Kitchen
scenes.prompt: Continue from dining into the exact kitchen shown in the reference. Begin beside the dining table and glide gently forward and slightly right, revealing the kitchen island, stools, cabinetry, worktops and window while preserving the dining composition behind. Maintain the same golden-hour light and material palette as the previous apartment shots. No object or furniture mutation. Finish with the kitchen clearly established while retaining a hint of the dining space for continuity.

scenes.name: Master Bedroom Hero
scenes.prompt: Reveal the exact master bedroom in the reference as the private emotional peak of the home tour. Begin near the doorway and slowly dolly inward with a gentle arc toward the bed and balcony glazing. Preserve bed, bedside tables, artwork, walk-in wardrobe, lounge chair, plants, lighting, textiles, balcony and skyline. Subtle curtain movement only. Serene premium mood, stable architecture, no furniture or text mutation. Finish oriented toward the balcony doors so the next shot can step outside.

scenes.name: Balcony Lifestyle View
scenes.prompt: Continue naturally from the bedroom onto the exact balcony shown in the reference. Make a very slow outward glide toward the glass railing and panoramic view, preserving balcony furniture, plants, candles, interior bedroom connection, skyline, water and landscape. Any person already visible should remain subtle with minimal natural motion. Let the sunset and distant city become the emotional focus. Finish holding on the horizon for a calm breath before the final exterior return.

scenes.name: Closing Exterior Hero
scenes.prompt: Return to the exact residential campus from the opening shot, but reverse the emotional direction for the finale. Begin closer to the landscaped heart and slowly rise and pull backward, revealing the complete development as evening lights glow. Preserve all tower and site geometry. Movement must be majestic but restrained, with clean stable architecture and soft atmospheric depth. Finish high and wide with uncluttered visual space suitable for the final Ninth Atlas title and end slate added later in editing.
